moat_against: Fragmented market — leader holds only single-digit share in smart water; no network effects
Much of the portfolio is engineered equipment contestable by Veralto, Pentair, Ecolab and local rivals
China business in retreat (orders collapsed; headcount cut ~40%)
Applied Water exposed to residential/commercial construction cycles
Serial-acquirer model: growth partly bought (Evoqua, now Cornell/Roper pumps) with integration and leverage risk
Metering (MCS) segment currently declining — electric-metering headwinds
moat_for: Largest pure-play water platform post-Evoqua; scale in treatment, transport and metering
Installed base drives recurring aftermarket, services and outsourced-water revenue
Sensus AMI metering specified into long utility replacement cycles (switching costs)
Proven pricing power — operating margin 13.3% → 16.7% YoY in Q2 2026 through tariff pressure
Regulatory demand drivers (PFAS remediation, IIJA funding) favor the incumbent leader
moat_justification: Largest pure-play water technology company after the 2023 Evoqua deal: installed equipment base with recurring aftermarket/service revenue, Sensus AMI metering positions specified into long utility cycles, a global service and distribution network across 50+ countries, and demonstrated pricing power (margins expanded through tariff pressure). Held below strong: the broader water market is fragmented (single-digit share even for the leader), much of the portfolio is engineered equipment contestable by Veralto, Pentair, Ecolab and local players, metering faces credible rivals, and returns are good rather than exceptional.
name: Xylem Inc.
one_liner: High-quality water pure-play, moat 6/10 — but priced for perfection on owner's earnings: weighted IRR 7.4% at $102.74, weighted IV@15% $38.44; clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$38.
